BiblicalUsage: This word means lion of God, and it is used for men, not places. Benaiah the son of Jehoiada slew two lionlike men of Moab, and both Samuel and Chronicles remember the deed the same way, as the mark of a hero.
TheologicalSignificance: One word for lionlike men carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the picture, that courage in battle was remembered as something lionlike, and God gave such men to Israel.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
